item.title: Extending immunity until 2027 in Constitution Bill is a typo and will be changed - Kamikamica
item.description: Immunity will not be extended until the first sitting of the new Parliament following the next general elections because of a typing error in the Constitution Amendment Bill. Deputy Prime Minister, Manoa Kamikamica says concerns that everyone would be protected until 2027 are nonsense.
item.content:encoded:
Immunity will not be extended until the first sitting of the new Parliament following the next general elections because of a typing error in the Constitution Amendment Bill.

Deputy Prime Minister, Manoa Kamikamica says concerns that everyone would be protected until 2027 are nonsense.

Kamikamica made this clear during the Fijian Media Association Town Hall Forum on the Constitution Amendment Bill at FNU Nasinu.

He stresses that there was a mistake in the draft which is still a Bill which will be amended.

Education Minister and SODELPA Leader Aseri Radrodro emphasised that the immunity clause should be removed as this is one of the reasons why the party is rejecting the Bill in the current form.

He says late former Prime Minister Laisenia Qarase initiated the affirmative action with iTaukei. and they see the 2013 Constitution as a weapon that was used to eliminate that affirmative action.

Government MP and Leader of the National Federation Party Professor Biman Prasad also stresses that they do not support any kind of immunity in any constitution.

He says there are people in this country who have supported coups and got away with them.

He says there should never be immunity for coup makers, those who enable coups, or those who form part of a coup government.

Fiji Labour Party Leader and former Prime Minister Mahendra Chaudhry also says the immunity clause should be completely out of the constitution.

When questioned that Professor Prasad was perhaps referring to him as someone who supported the 2006 coup, Chaudhry says his entry into the Bainimarama Government as Finance Minister was at the request of the President.

However, when pushed by fijivillage News Director Vijay Narayan and MaiTV Director Stanley Simpson that a coup is a coup and questioned if it should be justified, Chaudhry says Bainimarama took over the government because Qarase was pushing for the Reconciliation Bill, releasing the coup makers from prison and paying them while they were in prison, but Qarase did not listen.

It was also highlighted that the Commander of the Republic of Fiji Military Forces, Major General Ro Jone Kalouniwai had stated that they do not agree with the extension of the immunity to the new Parliament.

Unity Fiji Leader Savenaca Narube says they have always been against immunity as it sends the wrong signal to everybody in Fiji and reinforces the coup culture.

He says legal implications of removing immunity need to be examined but argues that there may be other ways to address the concerns without including immunity in the Constitution.

Opposition MP Premila Kumar says the Supreme Court’s opinion was to retain the 2013 Constitution, including Chapter 10, while opening the door to a process of constitutional change.

She says removing the 2013 Constitution would also remove Chapter 10, and it would be inconsistent to introduce a new Constitution with immunity provisions under Chapter 14.

Kumar says the Supreme Court’s decision must be read in its entirety and it is not fair to retain parts of the decision while disregarding others.

She says immunity should not be included in the 2026 Constitution if the Government is proceeding in line with the Supreme Court’s decision.

One Nation President Roko Tupou Draunidalo says the Supreme Court’s opinion to Cabinet is not a judgement or ruling and says it cannot bind Parliament or rewrite the Constitution.

She supports retaining the 2013 Constitution, including its immunity provisions, arguing that immunity was intended to enable a peaceful transfer of power from revolutionary governments through elections rather than continued conflict.

Kamikamica has stressed that the Court’s opinion is legally binding.

He says the Supreme Court has reasoned that if the immunity clause is removed, the Government, the two former Prime Ministers, the military, judges, civil servants and even Fiji Labour Party Leader Mahendra Chaudhry could face lawsuits because Chaudhry was part of the first Cabinet after the 2006 coup, potentially creating instability. The consultation on the Constitution Amendment Bill concludes this week, with a report expected to be tabled in Parliament next week and voting following the third reading.

item.title: FSC debt and rising costs put pressure on Govt spending “ Gounder
item.description: Fijians could face reduced funding for essential services such as housing, hospitals and education as rising debt servicing costs and financial pressures at the Fiji Sugar Corporation, alongside Government exposure to other state-owned enterprises including Fiji Airways, put pressure on public finances. This has been highlighted by Permanent Secretary for Finance Shiri Gounder during a panel discu
item.content:encoded:
Fijians could face reduced funding for essential services such as housing, hospitals and education as rising debt servicing costs and financial pressures at the Fiji Sugar Corporation, alongside Government exposure to other state-owned enterprises including Fiji Airways, put pressure on public finances.

This has been highlighted by Permanent Secretary for Finance Shiri Gounder during a panel discussion after World Bank Group Senior Economist Tihomir Stucka questioned what a credible path for Fiji would be to stabilise and eventually reduce its public debt.

Gounder says FSC is facing an extremely serious financial situation, with the Government guaranteeing more than $300 million in its debt and recently meeting the corporation's structural cash flow deficit.

He warns that if FSC's financial situation continues to deteriorate, the full fiscal exposure from its debt could fall on the Government.

He says rising debt servicing costs are reducing the amount of taxpayer money available for essential services, including housing, hospitals and education, and could also limit the Government's ability to respond to a future crisis.

Insert: Gounder on possible next crisis 29th Oct

Gounder says Government expenditure has grown by almost 40 percent in recent years, with a significant increase in operating expenditure contributing to a structural fiscal deficit of 7 percent this year.

He warns that without changes to the current approach, the Government could struggle to finance its budget.

Gounder says the growing fiscal deficit is also contributing to pressure on the current account and balance of payments, with exports remaining stagnant while imports continue to rise.

He says the Government needs to control expenditure growth and redirect funding from low-impact areas towards more productive investments.

Gounder also calls for a review of the size of the public sector , better targeting of social spending and subsidies, and measures to improve tax compliance and government revenue.

He says growing the economy and supporting the private sector would be the least painful way to address the country's fiscal challenges.

item.title: Stroke remains one of Fiji’s top three causes of death - Fong
item.description: Around 663 deaths per year are attributed to stroke, which accounts for roughly 13 percent of all deaths in Fiji and is consistently listed amongst the top three to four leading causes of death in Fiji. Speaking during the Counterstroke Fiji first anniversary, President for Counterstroke Fiji Elizabeth Fong says today is a day dedicated to raising awareness about stroke prevention, treatment and r
item.content:encoded:
Around 663 deaths per year are attributed to stroke, which accounts for roughly 13 percent of all deaths in Fiji and is consistently listed amongst the top three to four leading causes of death in Fiji.

Speaking during the Counterstroke Fiji first anniversary, President for Counterstroke Fiji Elizabeth Fong says today is a day dedicated to raising awareness about stroke prevention, treatment and recovery.

While speaking to Year 11 student, she says too many people between the ages of 40-60 are dying because of non-communicable diseases like stroke and diabetes.

Fong says the youths and students will help champion healthy behaviours within their families, schools, campuses and communities.

Fong says many of these conditions are linked to preventable risk factors such as chronic high blood presure, smoking, unhealthy diets physical inactivity, obesity and alcohol use.

She says recognising the signs early and taking medical attention can save lives.
